scenarios.label: Shift outdoor work hours
scenarios.detail: Move the working day to 06:00-11:00 and 17:00-21:00.
scenarios.basis: Exact: recomputed from the ISO 7243 / ACGIH hourly allowance.

scenarios.label: Shade over outdoor work areas
scenarios.detail: Tarpaulin or tree cover blocking 70% of direct sun.
scenarios.basis: Radiation term reduced; air temperature and humidity unchanged.

scenarios.label: Green the hottest neighbourhoods
scenarios.detail: Raise vegetation by 35% in the hottest 25% of zones (98 zones).
scenarios.basis: Measured across the treated zones only. Our offset is defined relative to the city mean, so this model cannot represent city-wide cooling -- and it inherits the ASSUMED amplitude, making this the least certain of the three.

actions.title: Stop outdoor work in the peak window
actions.detail: No safe outdoor work between 10:30 and 17:30.
actions.evidence: 8 hours at zero permitted work for heavy labour.

actions.title: Move shifts to the safe window
Concentrate relief at the daily peak
actions.detail: Heat stress peaks at 13:30; position water, shade and rest points before then.

actions.title: Check on the most vulnerable first
actions.detail: Lower safe limits apply to school child, woman.
actions.evidence: Reduced heat tolerance applied as a stated judgement.

omitted.why: Hydration is not a thermal quantity. Our model cannot estimate its effect, so it is not offered as though it could.
We have no population data and vulnerability is a declared placeholder. A precise headcount would be fabricated.
